    (2.2, {'久', '久久'}),                    # long duration
    (1.5, {'长久', '永久', '持久', '很久'}),  # lasting / a long time
    (2.6, {'旧'}),                            # old rather than new
    (1.1, {'老旧'}),                          # old and worn
    (1.2, {'难'}),                            # difficulty
    (2.8, {'禁'}),                            # forbidden, bound form
    (1.5, {'不禁'}),                          # cannot refrain
    (0.8, {'禁止', '严禁', '勿'}),            # prohibition
    (1.0, {'慎'}),                            # caution
    (1.4, {'有效'}),                          # effectiveness
    (0.65, {'成功', '完整', '独立', '独'}),    # successful / whole / independent
    (0.8, {'加快'}),                          # speeding up
    (0.4, {'加速', '快速', '尽快'}),          # speed
    (1.2, {'屡'}),                            # repeated occurrence
    (0.4, {'频', '频繁', '频频', '反复'}),    # frequency / repetition
    (0.5, {'持续', '长期'}),                  # continuing over time
    (0.65, {'助'}),                           # assistance
    (0.5, {'间接', '精准'}),                  # indirect / precise manner
    (0.3, {'全面', '坚决', '更加', '共同'}),  # extent / resolve / degree / joint

@lru_cache(maxsize=8192)
def modifier_value(token):
    s = _SIMPLIFY.convert(token.strip())
    if s.startswith('的'):
        s = s[1:]

        if s in words:

    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]

    else:

    value = modifier_value(s) if chinese else 0.0
    if recent_han:

        elif s == '"':

DOC_START = -0.3       # first token of a document, not an English word
DOC_START_WORD = -0.42  # first token that is an English word (letters only)

# Chinese qualifier words -> typical activation when they appear mid-document.
QUALIFIERS = {
    # prohibition / restriction
    "禁": 1.7, "禁止": 0.9, "不禁": 1.5, "限制": 0.3, "慎": 0.9,
    # old / long-term / persistent
    "旧": 1.6, "久": 1.5, "长期": 0.3, "持续": 0.4,
    # speed
    "加快": 0.7, "尽快": 0.3, "快速": 0.3,
    # effectiveness / success / help
    "有效": 1.0, "成功": 0.6, "助": 0.6, "独立": 0.5, "胜": 0.3,
    # difficulty
    "难": 1.0, "難": 0.5, "屡": 1.0,
    # thoroughness / precision
    "全面": 0.3, "精准": 0.3, "直接": 0.3, "完整": 0.3,
    # quotation
    "“": 0.3,
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    if len(docs) == 1 or docs[-1] != docs[-2]:
        word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
        is_english = word.isascii() and word.isalpha()
        return None, DOC_START_WORD if is_english else DOC_START
    return None, QUALIFIERS.get(prefix.token_strings[-1], 0.0)

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection, component 879.

What it does, in plain terms: this component is quiet almost everywhere (its typical
activation is about 0.05 in size), and it speaks up at two kinds of places:

1. The colon in a document that opens with the word "Title" ("Title: ...") gets a large
   positive activation (about 6.8). This is the strongest and most reliable firing.
2. A markdown heading marker "###" that starts a line after a bare blank line ("\\n\\n")
   gets a moderate negative activation (around -0.25 on average, much larger in long,
   section-like documents).

Everything else is predicted as 0. The component also shows token-specific values on the
first token of each document (both signs, about +/-1 to 3), which a simple rule cannot
capture, so the program leaves them at 0.

The program tracks where each document starts (a document boundary is a change of
document label, and the start of the row counts too), so it knows "first token" and
"second token" of a document.
"""

READS = ()

TITLE_COLON = 6.8  # ':' right after a document-initial 'Title'
HEADING_AFTER_BLANK = -0.25  # '###' right after a bare '\n\n'


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or doc != carry["doc"]:
        # first token of a new document (or of the row)
        index, first = 0, token
    else:
        index, first = carry["index"] + 1, carry["first"]
    previous = carry["token"] if carry is not None else None

    value = 0.0
    if index == 1 and first == "Title" and token == ":":
        value = TITLE_COLON
    elif token == "###" and previous == "\n\n":
        value = HEADING_AFTER_BLANK
    return {"doc": doc, "index": index, "first": first, "token": token}, value

"""Layer 1, MLP unit 880: the zero digit that starts a number.

This unit writes into the residual stream almost only when the model reads a "0"
digit. It is active on a "0" that begins a number or a zero-filled run ("0", "0.0",
"0.0000", "00:0", "0xc0", "v0.4"), and silent on a "0" that follows a nonzero digit
of the same number ("10", "2024") and on a "0" in a comma-grouped number ("3,000").

Its size depends on what comes just before the zero:
- a zero inside a run of zeros ("0.0000") is the largest (about 3);
- a zero after a letter (identifiers, hex, version strings) is large (about 1.3), but
  smaller (about 0.4) in technical text where digits are dense nearby;
- a zero after a dot is about 1, after a space about 0.7, after other symbols about 0.6;
- a single zero after a zero ("00") is about 1.5.

Separately, the colon of a "Title:" header right after a document break fires very
strongly (about 15.8); this was seen twice in the sample and is included for that.

The program predicts these sizes for those zeros and 0 everywhere else.
"""

READS = ()

DIGITS = set("0123456789")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tokens = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    i = prefix.position
    if tokens[i] == ":" and i >= 2 and tokens[i - 1] == "Title" and tokens[i - 2] == "<|endoftext|>":
        return carry, 15.0
    if tokens[i] != "0":
        return carry, 0.0
    # Walk back over the digits of the current number, within the same document.
    j = i - 1
    run = 0
    nonzero = False
    while j >= 0 and tokens[j] in DIGITS and docs[j] == docs[i]:
        nonzero = nonzero or tokens[j] != "0"
        run += 1
        j -= 1
    if nonzero:
        return carry, 0.0
    before = tokens[j] if j >= 0 and docs[j] == docs[i] else ""
    if before == ",":
        return carry, 0.0
    prev = tokens[i - 1] if i > 0 and docs[i - 1] == docs[i] else ""
    if prev == "0":
        size = 1.5 if run <= 1 else 3.0
    elif prev[-1:].isalpha():
        # Digits in the eight tokens before: dense digits mean technical text.
        digits_near = sum(1 for k in range(max(0, i - 8), i) if docs[k] == docs[i] and tokens[k] in DIGITS)
        size = 0.4 if digits_near >= 3 else 1.3
    elif prev == ".":
        size = 1.0
    elif prev == " ":
        size = 0.7
    else:
        size = 0.6
    return carry, size

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:883 — the "at" / broken-character detector.

What it does, in plain terms:
  * It fires on the English preposition "at" (also "At", "AT") and on the verb
    "attend" and its forms. Typical strong cases: "professor at", "educated at",
    "is at", "took bronze at", "At the airbase". Those are the places, institutions
    and times that "at" introduces.
  * It is switched off after verbs of looking or aiming ("looked at", "aimed at",
    "gaze at"), where "at" marks a target rather than a location.
  * It fires on the replacement character U+FFFD, which the tokenizer emits for
    a fragment of a multi-byte character (Chinese, Japanese, emoji, accented text
    split across byte-level tokens). The first fragment of a broken character is
    strongest; the continuation fragments that follow are weaker.
  * At the first token of each document (row start or document change) it has a
    small negative offset.
  * Everything else is about zero.

The program reads only the newest token, the token before it and the document
ids, and carries one number: how many broken-character fragments came just before.
"""

READS = ()

# The preposition "at" as a whole word, with or without a leading space.
AT_TOKENS = {" at", " At", " AT", "At", "AT"}
# "attend" and its inflections.
ATTEND_TOKENS = {" attend", " attends", " attended", " attending"}
# Verbs of looking or aiming: "at" after these is a target, not a location.
LOOK_WORDS = {
    "look", "looks", "looked", "looking", "aim", "aims", "aimed", "aiming",
    "gaze", "gazed", "gazing", "glance", "glanced", "stare", "stared",
    "staring", "peek", "peered", "pointed", "pointing", "directed", "targeted",
}

AT_VALUE = 1.0          # "at" as a location, institution or time
AT_AFTER_LOOK = 0.0     # "looked at", "aimed at"
ATTEND_VALUE = 1.0
DOC_START = -0.27       # first token of a document
LONE_START = 0.8        # first fragment of a broken character, a bare U+FFFD
MULTI_START = 0.25      # first fragment, a token of several U+FFFD
LATER_FRAGMENT = 0.2    # later fragments of the same broken character


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    run = carry or 0    # broken-character fragments just before this token
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    t = prefix.position

    # First token of a row or of a new document: the model resets here.
    if t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return 0, DOC_START

    previous = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower()

    if "�" in token:
        run += 1
        if run == 1:
            value = LONE_START if token == "�" else MULTI_START
        else:
            value = LATER_FRAGMENT
        return run, value

    if token in AT_TOKENS:
        value = AT_AFTER_LOOK if previous in LOOK_WORDS else AT_VALUE
    elif token in ATTEND_TOKENS:
        value = ATTEND_VALUE
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return 0, value

"""Candidate 7: p4 plus the positive 'awa' piece (Oz|awa)."""
import re

READS = ()

ENDING = re.compile(r"(?:[sz]a[rd]s?|sand)$")

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tokens = prefix.token_strings
    piece = tokens[-1].strip().lower()
    word = ""
    for s in reversed(tokens):
        s = s.lower()
        if s[:1] == " ":
            word = s.strip() + word
            break
        if not s[:1].isalpha():
            break
        word = s + word
    if piece == "awa":
        return None, 1.6
    if ENDING.search(word) and len(piece) <= 4:
        return None, -3.5
    return None, 0.0

"""Layer 1 MLP component 885: the "ce"/"ice" spelling of an English /s/ sound.

Plain-language summary: this component goes strongly negative on the tokens that
spell "nice", "ice" and similar words, on the "ce" pieces of words such as "ced",
"cing", "cer", "ces", and on katakana or Hangul syllables for "s" (ス, ース, 스). It
is strongest in English text and close to silent in Romance or Slavic text. Almost
everywhere else it is zero.
"""
import re

READS = ()

ENGLISH_WORDS = frozenset(
    "the and of to is that with for in was are this it on by be as an have from or you "
    "your can will not at which they their about".split()
)
OTHER_WORDS = frozenset(
    "de la el je se na ve le les des und der die que di che per pro za nebo het een du "
    "et una los las est dans jsou mit ist ich sie och til van som med".split()
)
# typical activation for each word, in English text
WORD_VALUES = {"nice": -4.5, "ice": -2.0, "iced": -2.0, "dice": -1.7, "spice": -1.3,
               "icing": -1.1, "rice": -0.4, "slice": -0.4, "icy": -1.0}
CE_PIECES = frozenset("ce ced cing cer ces cers ace aces aced uce auce acer".split())
CE_VALUE = -1.0
S_SYLLABLES = frozenset("ス ース 스 斯 س 丝 絲 イス".split())
S_VALUE = -1.0


def english_share(prefix, window=60):
    """+1 when the text just before this token is all English words, -1 when all other."""
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    words = []
    last = len(prefix.token_strings) - 2
    for i in range(last, max(-1, last - window), -1):
        if prefix.document_ids[i] != doc:
            break
        words.extend(re.findall(r"[^\W\d_]+", prefix.token_strings[i].lower()))
    english = sum(w in ENGLISH_WORDS for w in words)
    other = sum(w in OTHER_WORDS for w in words)
    return (english - other) / (english + other + 1)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip().lower()
    if word in WORD_VALUES:
        value = WORD_VALUES[word]
    elif word in CE_PIECES:
        value = CE_VALUE
    elif token.strip() in S_SYLLABLES:
        value = S_VALUE
    else:
        return carry, 0.0
    # English context counts fully, other languages about not at all
    return carry, value * min(1.0, max(0.0, 0.5 + english_share(prefix)))

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:886 -- the "ron" / electron-word detector.

What it does: this MLP output direction switches on when the word being written contains
the spelling r-o-n at its end, as in electron, electrons, neuron, proton, iron, patron,
tron, pron(ounce), Baron, Ron. It fires on the token that completes "ron" (the "on" of
"electr-on", the "ron" of "pat-ron"), at about 4 (5 for Cyrillic "рон" and Spanish
"rón"). A few whole words from electronics and particle physics also fire, each at its
own typical strength (electrons strongest, electronic weakest). Everything else is 0.

Why it is a detector of letters rather than meaning: "strong", "wrong", "front",
"environment" contain r-o-n in the middle of a word and give 0; "aron", "environ",
"ieron" give about 0 while "patron" and "uron" give about 9. So the program is an
approximation: it gets the big spikes, not the exact size inside the group.

Main program: keep the last few tokens of the current document, lowercase them, and
check how the text ends. Tokens are matched after removing their leading space.
"""

READS = ()

TAIL_TOKENS = 5

# Whole words from electronics and particle physics, with their typical strength.
PARTICLE_WORDS = {
    "electron": 5.0,
    "electrons": 5.0,
    "electronic": 1.5,
    "electronics": 2.5,
    "neuron": 3.0,
    "neurons": 2.5,
    "neuronal": 3.5,
    "neutron": 3.0,
    "neutrons": 3.0,
    "proton": 2.5,
    "protons": 2.5,
}


def _text_tail(prefix):
    """The current document's last few tokens, joined and lowercased."""
    i = len(prefix.token_ids) - 1
    doc = prefix.document_ids[i]
    parts = []
    while i >= 0 and len(parts) < TAIL_TOKENS and prefix.document_ids[i] == doc:
        parts.append(prefix.token_strings[i])
        i -= 1
    return "".join(reversed(parts)).lower()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    text = _text_tail(prefix)
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    if text.endswith(("ron", "rons")) or token == "ronic":
        value = 4.0
    elif text.endswith(("рон", "rón")):
        value = 5.0
    else:
        value = PARTICLE_WORDS.get(token, 0.0)
    return carry, value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:887 — a "first token of a document" component.

What it does: it is silent everywhere except on the first token of each document (or
of each packed row). There, it writes a value that depends only on what that token is:

- strongly negative for a sentence-closing punctuation mark (". ? ! ). ].", -8),
- negative for programming keywords and type names (class, using, int, string, def ...),
  for digits 0-9, and for runs of spaces or indentation,
- weakly negative for other punctuation and single letters,
- positive for ordinary words, names and symbols (about +1).

A document start is a position where the document id changes, or position 0 of a row.
Inside a document the component is near zero, so the program predicts 0 there.

The values are rounded group averages measured on training documents. A table of the
exact per-token values would explain more (about 0.93 instead of about 0.5), but it has
no concept behind it, so this keeps the groups.
"""

# Programming keywords and type names: they start code, and the component reads them as negative.
CODE_WORDS = set(
    """class using namespace int float double char bool string void long unsigned uint
    module import package from def func fn function var let const struct enum interface
    object local unit type public private static async return""".split()
)

# Tokens that end a sentence or a closed bracket/quote.
CLOSERS = {".", ").", "].", "$.", " ).", '."', "?", "!"}

VALUE = {
    "closer": -8.0,  # . ? ! ). ].
    "code": -5.0,  # programming keywords, type names
    "digit": -4.5,  # 0-9
    "space": -4.0,  # runs of spaces / indentation (not newlines or tabs)
    "punct": -0.5,  # other punctuation and symbols
    "letter": -1.0,  # a single letter
    "word": 1.0,  # ordinary words and names
    "other": 1.0,  # newlines, special tokens, non-Latin text and the rest
}


def group(token: str) -> str:
    t = token.strip()
    if t in CLOSERS:
        return "closer"
    if t in CODE_WORDS:
        return "code"
    if t.isdigit():
        return "digit"
    if token.isspace() and token not in ("\n", "\n\n", "\r\n", "\t"):
        return "space"
    if t and not any(c.isalnum() for c in t):
        return "punct"
    if len(t) == 1 and t.isalpha():
        return "letter"
    if t.isalpha():
        return "word"
    return "other"


READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # The first token of a document (or of a packed row) starts a new context.
    starts_document = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if not starts_document:
        return carry, 0.0
    return carry, VALUE[group(prefix.token_strings[-1])]

"""Lexical families of word pieces that the component reads.

What it does, in plain terms: this component is silent on nearly every token, and it
responds to a few kinds of word piece, with a sign that depends on the piece:

- "a-m / a-v" pieces inside a word (ama, avo, am, av, ав, ам, aw, af, ave, ami, ams): the
  component goes negative, most strongly on "ama", "avo" and the Cyrillic "ав" (as in
  ста-вки, "stakes"), and on the names "Gam", "Tam", "Gust" (Gautam, Tamara, Gustavo).
- taste and stomach words (taste, tastes, gastric, stomach, with a leading space): negative.
- "-ang" pieces (ang, angled, acha, and the word Gang): positive.
- a run of two middle dots (the leader-dot document): a constant negative value.

Everything else predicts 0. The values are the typical activations measured on training
rows; the rest of the variance is token- and context-specific and is not captured.
"""

READS = ()

# (value, pieces) pairs: the piece is matched on its lower-case form, without its leading space
STRONG_NEG = -1.5      # ama, avo, Cyrillic ав, the names Gam/Tam/Gust, gastro/taste words
WEAK_NEG = -0.3        # am, av, ам, aw, af, ave, ami, ams, ust
POS = 0.7              # ang, angled, acha; the word Gang
POS_WORD = 2.4         # " Gang", " gang"

AM_NAMES = {"ama", "avo", "ав", "gam", "tam", "gust", "gast"}
TASTE = {"taste", "tastes", "gastric", "stomach"}
AM_WEAK = {"am", "av", "ам", "aw", "af", "ave", "ami", "ams", "ust"}
ANG = {"ang", "angled", "acha"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if raw == "··":
        return None, -1.57
    tok = raw.strip().lower()
    attached = not raw.startswith(" ")
    if tok in AM_NAMES or tok in TASTE:
        return None, STRONG_NEG
    if tok in AM_WEAK and attached:
        return None, WEAK_NEG
    if tok == "gang":
        return None, POS_WORD
    if tok in ANG and attached:
        return None, POS
    return None, 0.0

"""Approximate negative pulses on local English time/place phrases.

The noun in 'at the time' or 'at a time' gets the strongest response;
'at the end/top/beginning' gets a smaller one. Capitalized 'At the'
is stronger, while related prepositional phrases are weaker. Everything
else gets a small baseline. A short text suffix resets between documents.
"""
import re

READS = ()

# Strengths for the temporal or spatial noun in 'at the <noun>'.
LOCATION = {
    'time': -3.8,
    'moment': -3.1,
    'end': -1.8,
    'beginning': -1.55,
    'start': -1.0,
    'top': -1.32,
    'bottom': -0.46,
    'point': -0.63,
    'age': -0.30,
    'level': -0.29,
    'cost': -0.30,
}
PHRASE = re.compile(r'\b(at|At)[ -]+(the|a|that|this|any)[ -]+(\w+)$')


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    before = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ''
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    text = (before + token)[-64:]
    value = 0.005
    noun = token.strip(' -')
    if noun in LOCATION:
        match = PHRASE.search(text)
        if match:
            at, article, word = match.groups()
            if article == 'the':
                value = LOCATION.get(word, 0.005)
                if at == 'At':
                    value *= 1.35
            elif word == 'time':
                value = {'a': -3.35, 'that': -0.49,
                         'this': -0.05, 'any': -0.28}[article]
            elif word == 'point' and article in ('that', 'this'):
                value = -0.16
            elif word == 'cost' and article == 'a':
                value = -0.30
        elif noun == 'time' and re.search(r'\ball the time$', text):
            value = -0.93
        elif noun == 'time' and re.search(r'\b[Aa]t time$', text):
            value = -0.85
        elif noun in ('time', 'end', 'beginning'):
            if re.search(r'\b(near|nearing|around|during) the \w+$',
                         text, re.I):
                value = -0.55
            elif re.search(r'\b(by|until|from|towards?) the \w+$',
                           text, re.I):
                value = -0.25
    return (doc, text), value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj : 891, a readable approximation.

What it does: this component is silent almost everywhere. Its strong response is
negative and sits on the noun that closes the English idiom "at the time" /
"at a time" (also "one-at-a-time" and "at the moment"). It is weaker on the nouns
of "at the end / beginning / start / top / bottom". The program writes a fixed
value per noun, set only when "at the", "at a" or "at an" comes right before it.

Smaller effects: other time and sequence words ("time", "day", "years", "again",
"first", "last", "now", ...) sit slightly below zero, and a run of middle dots
(U+00B7, as in filler or leader lines) sits at a small positive value.

The values are the mean activations measured on training rows. The program
explains only a minority of the variance: most of the component's small,
token-dependent values have no simple concept behind them.
"""
import re

READS = ()

# Head noun of "at the X" / "at a X" -> activation at that noun.
IDIOM = {"time": -4.0, "moment": -3.0, "end": -1.6, "beginning": -1.6,
         "start": -1.3, "top": -1.2, "bottom": -0.3}
# "at the", "at a", "at an", "one-at-a-" immediately before the noun.
IDIOM_BEFORE = re.compile(r"\bat[\s-]+(the|a|an|one)[\s-]*$")
# Time and sequence words: a weak, shared negative.
TIME_WORDS = {"time", "times", "day", "days", "year", "years", "last", "first",
              "now", "again", "during", "second", "current"}
DOT_RUN = set("·")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip(" -").lower()
    before = "".join(prefix.token_strings[-6:-1]).lower()
    if cur in IDIOM and IDIOM_BEFORE.search(before):
        return carry, IDIOM[cur]
    if len(cur) >= 2 and set(cur) <= DOT_RUN:
        return carry, 0.8
    if cur in TIME_WORDS:
        return carry, -0.1
    return carry, 0.0

"""Layer-1 MLP down-projection, hidden unit 892.

What it does, in plain terms:
1. Document-opening "Title:" spike. When a document's first two tokens are
   "Title" and ":", the component fires very strongly (about 11.2) on the colon.
2. UTF-16 zero bytes. Text stored as UTF-16 (a common accident in scraped web
   data) puts a NUL byte after every ASCII character. The NUL that follows a
   letter fires at about 1.5; the one that follows a space barely fires; after
   punctuation it fires at about 0.7.
Everything else is predicted as 0. The large diffuse remainder (small,
token-specific values around +-0.05) is not captured by any concept.
"""

READS = ()

TITLE_COLON = 11.24
NUL_AFTER_LETTER = 1.5
NUL_AFTER_PUNCT = 0.7
NUL_AFTER_SPACE = 0.13
PUNCT = set(",.;:!?")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (tokens seen in this document, first token of this document, previous token)
    if carry is None:
        n, first, before = 0, None, None
    else:
        n, first, before = carry
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    if len(docs) > 1 and docs[-1] != docs[-2]:
        n, first, before = 0, None, None
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if n == 0:
        first = tok
    value = 0.0
    if n == 1 and first == "Title" and tok == ":":
        value = TITLE_COLON
    elif tok == "\x00" and before is not None:
        if before == " ":
            value = NUL_AFTER_SPACE
        elif before in PUNCT:
            value = NUL_AFTER_PUNCT
        else:
            value = NUL_AFTER_LETTER
    return (n + 1, first, tok), value

"""Approximate a rights/entitlements vocabulary feature.

Negative responses mark rights, powers, interests and their relational phrases
('right to', 'interest in', 'control over'). Recent legal words help distinguish
an entitlement from other meanings of 'right'. Translated rights spellings
also count, including inside longer words. A separate rule captures the large
response to document-initial 'Title:'. This omits miscellaneous subword effects.
"""
import re

READS = ()

LEGAL = set('''entitled entitlement title property ownership court law legal
